finding: Native danger reactions used a roof veto for prone rolls and two horizontal obstruction segments for upright lateral actions, but neither established lateral footing. An exposed ledge could pass the obstruction-only gate.
sourceIntent: Retain the LAMBS doDodge intent of a short immediate native reaction under fire while refusing sparse geometry that cannot support it. Do not copy unconditional forward/back actions or introduce a second route owner.
implementation: One shared actor-local CODE path computes a two-metre left/right sample. Two horizontal body-height segments reject obstructions, then midpoint/endpoint downward probes require terrain/ROADWAY support within0.75m of the original foot height and upward normal>=0.7. Actors/vehicles cannot be footing.

Both original prone roll and upright tactical action call it only after existing feature, owner, actor/native task, movement, weapon-state and cooldown gates. Prone retains its existing overhead veto. Refused lateral attempts consume the original3s cooldown. Posture fallback remains.

No world/roster scan, new movement instruction, replacement direction search, worker, task, setting, artificial animation, velocity or position write. Shared implementation replaces duplicate upright geometry.

cost.upright: At most2 existing horizontal rays plus2 new downward probes per eligible original3s attempt; short-circuits on obstruction/first unsupported point.
cost.prone: Existing overhead ray plus at most2 horizontal/2 downward probes after eligibility; overhead refusal remains the existing path.

limitations: Sparse samples are safety vetoes, not swept-body clearance, native animation displacement or pathfinding proof. Narrow/unsampled holes may remain.
Bounds intentionally refuse steep stairs/drops and unknown/missing walkable model surfaces; posture is retained rather than forcing movement.
Physical normal/HC, terrain/bridge/roof/stair/modded model responses and5%median/10%p95 overhead remain unverified. Audits paused.
